AUTHOR: Poling
TITLE: Annotation strategy trade-offs for deep learning-based underwater fish detection
REGION: Southern and western Norwegian coast; Skagerrak and Kattegat (Sweden)
SPECIES: Labrids (corkwing, goldsinny, ballan, cuckoo, rock cook), gadids (cod incl. YOY, pollack, saithe, whiting, haddock, poor cod), spiny dogfish, gobies, ling, decapods
DATA: FjordFish dataset (BRUV/RUV surveys 2018-2024; 3,002 images, 6,350 annotations, 27 classes) + separate test set of 200 images from unseen videos
V_EV: Sec. 2.2: 'Footage is primarily captured in shallow water (0–30 m)'; Sec. 4.2: gadids 'were more common in more turbid conditions in this dataset'
D2: Final models: expert-curated 2/3 train, 1/3 val (not spatially separated); test set 200 images from previously unseen videos; model selection by 6-fold 75/25 random image CV
D_EV: Sec. 2.1: 'A separate test dataset was also compiled from previously unseen videos'; Sec. 4.2 discusses 'risk of data leakage' in the train/val split
R_EV: Sec. 2.2: test set compiled 'to include annotations from unseen videos from more recent rounds of surveys' of the same FjordFish programme
C_EV: no statement found (default hyperparameters; no confidence threshold value reported)
E_EV: Sec. 4.3: 'performance metrics... (mAP50–95, F1 score etc.)... do not provide complete insight on how a model will perform compared to human annotators on full videos'
ARCH: YOLOv8m/x, YOLOv9c/e, YOLOv10b/x, YOLO11l/x; YOLOv9c selected; generalist vs specialist detectors
METR: Precision, recall, mAP50, mAP50-95, F1, weighted rank; zero-inflated beta regression of F1 on annotations
NOTE: Abstract headline figures are validation-based (expert split, images from same stations/videos can be in train and val - leakage acknowledged), but final models are also evaluated on a video-independent test set; D coded on the test design (영상). Test set comes from more recent survey rounds of the same FjordFish programme with some new conditions; year not stated -> R1=N per P2 (a verifier could code R1=Y/계절·시기 with R3=Y, since val and test metrics are both given, e.g. general gadids F1 0.691 val vs 0.427 test). Some cod annotations from a semi-natural mesocosm. An informal test on 50 unseen videos is mentioned qualitatively only. Trained model weights released on HuggingFace (no code repository stated).
